import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report is done; now checking the raw file for frontmatter and the infographic before restructuring.

External links are fine (the Apple thread hits a bot-check redirect, so I'm keeping it as unverified). Recording the infographic read, then writing the restructured report.

Written. Now validating anchors, list rendering under pandoc's default reader, URL coverage, and a word-level diff against the lead's report.

Content check is clean: every difference is an intended edit (added anchor links, parentheticals moved out of headings). Registering the artifact now.

Registration succeeded. Finishing with the final declaration.

I published the canonical report as `202610/research_swarm_listen_link/research_swarm_listen_link.md` in the research repo. It's registered as `file:explicit:a1249ad4f3acce1e23504a50`, and the host commits it when this turn ends.

**Opening:** The file opens with the lead's title, then a new one-blockquote research query, then the infographic, then `## Bottom line`. The infographic is `research_swarm_listen_link_infographic.png`, which I confirmed sits beside the report. The report has no frontmatter, so there was no `updated_time` to update.

**Restructure:**
- I kept the lead's order: Bottom line → How it works today → Critique → Requirement adjustments → Recommended solution.
- I moved "How the four reports were reconciled" down next to "Rejected alternatives" under a new `## Alternatives considered` section, since both cover options that lost.
- The lead's own "Research request" restatement is kept in a new section, `## The request as briefed`, just before Sources.
- Four headings had parenthetical text: "(verified)", "(called out)", "(one real swarm)" and "(not needed for v1)". I moved that text into each section's first line so the headings work as link targets.
- I added blank lines before several lists that pandoc's default Markdown reader would otherwise have run into the paragraph above. No wording changed.
- I added a few in-document links, to `#recommended-solution`, `#requirement-adjustments`, `#what-the-reader-sees` and `#follow-ups`.

**Checks:**
- **Anchors:** every one resolves under both pandoc's Markdown reader and its GitHub-flavored reader.
- **Content:** a word-level comparison against `__final.md` shows no lost claims, numbers, tables, code blocks or sources. The only differences are the added links and the heading edits above.
- **URLs:** the new file has exactly the same set as `__final.md`. Six of the seven returned 200.
  - The Apple Community thread (`discussions.apple.com/thread/251142029`) redirects to a human-verification page, so it's unverified. I kept the link as written.
- **Unrepairable links:** none.

**Listen line:** there is no `<name>_narration.mp3` in the folder; the audio agent committed only `_narration.md`. So the report has no listen line, which matches how the swarm works today.
